request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several of them. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V26__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table (from-date, optional to-date, one row per hold) and drops the old `held` column. Anyone who was on hold before this change gets an open-ended hold starting `0001-01-01`, so their hold works exactly as it did. It will show that placeholder date as its start.

**Server:**
- The hold endpoint now adds a hold instead of switching it on and off. A blank from-date means the sheet's today and a blank to-date means the hold never ends. A badly formed date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused and writes nothing.
- The audit line is `PERSON_HELD … name=<name> from=<date>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines when the figures move. `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone, since a hold now ends on its to-date.
- A claim is left out of the totals only if it is OPEN or PENDING, not bound by a statement, and dated within one of the person's holds. Everything else counts as before. The new check is `Person.counts(claim)`, and the rollup, the statement and period closing all use it.

**Front end:**
- "Hold yes/no" now means the person has any hold at all.
- Each hold is listed on the person's row, followed by the from and to boxes and the Hold button. The error shows on a refused hold and clears as soon as either box is edited.
- The totals on the page apply the same rule as the server.

One thing to be aware of: a PENDING claim isn't treated as bound by a statement anywhere in the app, so a stated PENDING claim dated within a hold is still left out. The tests don't cover that case.
